items.stem: A service runs now but does not start after reboot. Which action makes it start at boot?

options.text: Enable the service with systemctl enable
options.rationale: Correct: enabling creates the boot-time symlink so it starts on reboot.

options.text: Start the service with systemctl start
options.rationale: Starting runs it now but does not persist across reboot.
A manual run does not register the service for boot.
The hostname file is unrelated to service startup.

items.explanation: Correct: enabling creates the boot-time symlink so it starts on reboot.

items.stem: A persistent mount must survive reboot. Where should it be defined?

options.rationale: Correct: /etc/fstab defines mounts applied at boot.

options.text: Only via a one-time mount command
options.rationale: A manual mount does not persist across reboot.
Shell startup files do not configure system mounts.
The hosts file maps names to addresses, not mounts.

items.explanation: Correct: /etc/fstab defines mounts applied at boot.

items.stem: A web page returns a permission error though file permissions look correct on an SELinux-enforcing host. Which TWO steps are appropriate? (Select TWO)

options.text: Check and correct the SELinux file context
options.rationale: Correct: a wrong SELinux context blocks access despite correct DAC permissions.

options.text: Review SELinux denials in the audit log
options.rationale: Correct: audit denials reveal exactly what SELinux blocked.

options.text: Set SELinux to permissive permanently to fix it
options.rationale: Disabling enforcement removes protection instead of fixing the context.
Deleting content does not resolve a context problem.

items.explanation: Correct: a wrong SELinux context blocks access despite correct DAC permissions. Correct: audit denials reveal exactly what SELinux blocked.
